laws.rule: Picos de Europa National Park: the park’s detailed FAQ says camping is limited to authorised campsites or near villages with the owner’s permission. It describes bivouac without a tent above 1,800 m for mountain traverses, with exceptions, and tents only in adverse weather or force majeure. The same page retains an older 1,600 m summary, so confirm the current regional rules and location with the park.

Picos de Europa National Park: the park’s FAQ says fires are prohibited apart from controlled park-management work, and swimming in lakes and rivers is prohibited. Its general summary mentions possible designated bathing areas, so check local signs and current park guidance.

Wild mushroom picking in Castile and León: on forest land that has not been fenced off as a regulated picking area (acotado) or reserved by the owner, picking is for recreation or own use only. It needs no permit, but you may not take more than 3 kg of wild mushrooms per person per day, may not sell them, and may not pick truffles (article 13.4 and 13.5). Where an owner has set up a permit system, recreational permits can allow at most 5 kg per person per day (article 18). Picking at night (sunset to sunrise), digging up the soil, carrying rakes, hoes or similar tools, and using plastic bags or buckets are banned; baskets must be rigid or semi-rigid and let air through (article 8). Picking on road verges and along railways is banned (8.2.h). Carrying more than 10 kg needs the permit or proof of the owner's mushroom rights (article on transport). Read as published in the regional bulletin on 9 October 2017; later amendments were not checked.
